title: Superconducting qubit based on altermagnets
authors: Xue-Feng Pan, Xin-Lei Hei, Franco Nori, Peng-Bo Li
abstract: Altermagnets, characterized by vanishing net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin splitting, provide a promising platform for next-generation Josephson devices. Here, we exploit the Josephson effect in superconductor-altermagnet-superconductor junctions and show how to engineer prescribed current-phase relations by device design. Based on these programmable Josephson potentials utilizing altermagnetism, we propose a new class of transmon-like superconducting qubits that combine large anharmonicity with enhanced robustness against decoherence via coherent two-Cooper-pair tunneling. We show that in the $2φ$-junction regime, this kind of qubit provides intrinsic protection against charge noise due to parity protection. Magnetic flux can be used to precisely control the qubit and, under appropriate bias, this architecture further suppresses charge and flux noise. Our results establish altermagnets as a versatile platform for Josephson-potential engineering and open a new route toward high-performance superconducting qubits combining high coherence, large anharmonicity, and broad tunability.
summary: This paper proposes using superconducting junctions incorporating altermagnets to create next-generation qubits. By engineering the Josephson potential to include higher harmonics via double-Cooper-pair tunneling, the resulting qubit achieves large anharmonicity and intrinsic protection against charge noise. This establishes altermagnets as a programmable platform for high-coherence quantum computing components.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of engineering superconducting qubits with superior coherence and anharmonicity by designing novel Josephson potentials.
main_result: Altermagnets provide a versatile platform to engineer non-sinusoidal Josephson potentials, leading to transmon-like qubits that exhibit intrinsic protection against charge noise in the 2φ-junction regime.
method: The authors employ theoretical modeling, including calculating Josephson currents via the Furusaki-Tsukada formula and using inverse-design workflows to map target Current-Phase Relations (CPRs) to microscopic material parameters.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting qubit implemented using superconducting-altermagnet-superconductor junctions (AMJJs). The physics is governed by the Josephson energy, which can be engineered to contain both single- and double-Cooper-pair tunneling terms, leading to a potential $V(\phi) = -I_1 \cos(\phi) - I_2/2 \cos(2\phi)$.
key_observables: Qubit anharmonicity ($\alpha_f$), charge noise decay rates ($\Gamma_{Q}^{DC}, \Gamma_{Q}^{DP}$), and flux noise sensitivity ($\Gamma_{	ext{Flux}}^{DP}$).
important_parameters: The ratio $\eta = I_2/I_1$ dictates the junction regime ($\phi$, $0$, or $2\phi$), and external magnetic flux ($\Phi_{	ext{ext}}$) is used for fine-tuning.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating the system as a transmon-like qubit shunted by a capacitor, and the noise suppression mechanisms are derived from parity selection rules applied to the Cooper-pair number operator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the AMJJ and qubit circuit, the engineered Josephson potentials for different junction regimes, and the dependence of qubit properties (anharmonicity, noise coupling) on the junction parameters $\eta$ and external flux.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform (AMJJs) and the resulting programmable Josephson potential, to analyzing the resulting qubit Hamiltonian, and finally detailing the noise suppression mechanisms achieved through specific junction regimes (especially the $2\phi$-junction).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it proposes a solid-state, material-based route to overcome fundamental limitations in superconducting qubit coherence, directly impacting the feasibility of quantum computation hardware.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic of an AMJJ, consisting of an altermagnetic layer of thickness L sandwiched between two s-wave superconduc- tors. (b) Schematic of a transmon-like superconducting qubit circuit based on the AMJJ. Panels (c-e) schematically illustrate the Joseph- son energy corresponding to the ϕ-, 0-, and 2ϕ-junction realized with the AMJJ, respectively. The blue, red, and yellow shaded regions represent the wave-function distributions of the three lowest-energy eigenstates, respectively, while their vertical positions indicate the corresponding eigenenergies.

FIG. 2. (a, c) Modulation of the AMJJ Josephson energy by the alter- magnet thickness L and a chemical-potential mismatch δµ, respec- tively. (b, d) Corresponding harmonic components of the Josephson current for the cases shown in panels (a) and (c), respectively. The fixed parameters are J = 0.4µ, δµ = 0, and Z = 0 in panels (a, b), and J = 0.4µ, kF L = 20, and Z = 0 in panels (c, d).

FIG. 3. (a) Eigenenergy spectrum of the superconducting qubit as a function of η for EJ/EC = 50. The red star marks the critical value ηc, at which the first and second excited states become degen- erate. (b) Anharmonicity αf and (c) transverse charge-noise cou- pling strength N Q DC as functions of η for different values of EJ/EC. The stars in (c) mark the corresponding critical values ηc for different values of EJ/EC. (d) Wave functions of the ground and first excited states in the Cooper-pair-number ( ˆ N) basis for EJ/EC = 50. The blue and green dashed curves correspond to η = 0 and η = ηc, re- spectively.

FIG. 4. (a) Qubit transition frequency, (b) anharmonicity, (c) trans- verse charge-noise coupling strength N Q DC, and (d) longitudinal flux- noise coupling strength N Flux DP as functions of the external flux ϕext and the ratio η. The fixed parameters are EJ/EC = 50 and Ng = 0.
